answerNotes.ANGEL: Heavenly messenger in Bible stories. This scene follows Luke 1:26–38; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.

answerNotes.MARY: Mary is named as Jesus' mother in the Gospels. A story's setting helps distinguish her from other women named Mary.
answerNotes.JOSEPH: Joseph is Mary's husband in these Gospel scenes. He is a different person from Jacob's son in the Genesis stories.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.
answerNotes.WRAP: Wrap means put a covering around something. Paper is common for parcels and shop goods, while cloth can also be a wrapping material.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.MOTHER: Mother names a female parent. In a story scene, the surrounding names help show which family relationship is being described.
answerNotes.MANGER: Feeding trough used as a baby's bed in Luke. This scene follows Luke 2:1–7; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.BETHLEHEM: Town where Jesus was born. This scene follows Luke 2:1–7; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.ANGEL: Messenger from heaven. This scene follows Luke 2:8–20; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.SHEEP: Sheep are farm animals valued for wool and other products. A lamb is a young sheep, and an ewe is an adult female.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.PEACE: Peace can describe calm instead of conflict or disturbance. In the storm story, the setting concerns wind and water becoming still.

answerNotes.MYRRH: Myrrh is a fragrant resin, one of the gifts named in Matthew's wise-men story. It is not another name for gold.
answerNotes.KING: King can mean a ruler or a face card representing one. In a card deck, it belongs to a suit rather than ruling a country.
answerNotes.HOUSE: A house is a building. Home is the place associated with living and belonging, which need not be a separate house.
